title: ANTiC: Adaptive Neural Temporal In Situ Compressor
claim: A two-stage streaming pipeline first filters informative time steps, then compresses each selected one into compact neural weights for storage.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, gray block arrows linking stages, check/cross gate icons
description: A horizontal three-stage pipeline with gray block arrows between stages. Each stage has a gray title tab. On the left, Physics-aware Temporal Selector shows three 3D volume renderings of a field at t0, t1 and t2, where two bright blobs merge into one in warm orange-purple colors. Below is a Gate-Regulator plot with a sigmoid-like curve and three dashed threshold lines, one per time step. Green checkmarks mark t1 and t2 as selected, and a red cross marks t0 as rejected. A bent arrow leads to the middle panel, Spatial Neural Compression, a light-blue box with a small MLP taking x, y, z as input and outputting f(x,y,z). The right panel, Weight Storage, shows stacked code-like pages with params, layer_1 and layer_2 weights and biases.
caption: \textbf{Figure 1: Schematic Overview of \method{}.} \method{} facilitates high-fidelity neural compression via a dual-stage asynchronous architecture. Physics-aware Temporal Selector serves as a physics-aware filter that identifies salient physical transients. Spatial Neural Compression encodes the selected snapshots into compact NN weights, stored in the persistent storage. \method{} enables a combined in-situ compression resulting in multi-fold reduction in data volume while preserving the temporal coherence of the entire simulation.
abstract: The persistent storage requirements for high-resolution, spatiotemporally evolving fields governed by large-scale and high-dimensional partial differential equations (PDEs) have reached the petabyte-to-exabyte scale. Transient simulations modeling Navier-Stokes equations, magnetohydrodynamics, plasma physics, or binary black hole mergers generate data volumes that are prohibitive for modern high-performance computing (HPC) infrastructures. To address this bottleneck, we introduce ANTIC (Adaptive Neural Temporal in situ Compressor), an end-to-end in situ compression pipeline. ANTIC consists of an adaptive temporal selector tailored to high-dimensional physics that identifies and filters informative snapshots at simulation time, combined with a spatial neural compression module based on continual fine-tuning that learns residual updates between adjacent snapshots using neural fields. By operating in a single streaming pass, ANTIC enables a combined compression of temporal and spatial components and effectively alleviates the need for explicit on-disk storage of entire time-evolved trajectories. Experimental results demonstrate how storage reductions of several orders of magnitude relate to physics accuracy.
